### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease dominant intermediate E  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:23791)

**Proposed mechanism:** INF2 (HGNC:23791) —DISRUPTS→ Actin cytoskeleton organization and dynamics (GO:0016043); Actin cytoskeleton organization and dynamics (GO:0016043) —LEADS_TO→ Peripheral neuropathy (HP:0003198); Actin cytoskeleton organization and dynamics (GO:0016043) —LEADS_TO→ Foot malformation (HP:0001800); Actin cytoskeleton organization and dynamics (GO:0016043) —LEADS_TO→ Pes cavus (HP:0001491). Mutations in INF2 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting actin cytoskeleton organization and dynamics. This disruption underlies the shared phenotypic features of peripheral neuropathy and foot malformations, including pes cavus, observed in both MONDO:0013191 and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease dominant intermediate E (MONDO:0013758).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in INF2 with loss-of-function effects in individuals with MONDO:0013191 and gain-of-function effects in individuals with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease dominant intermediate E (MONDO:0013758) would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in INF2 with allele frequency >0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of INF2 in these two distinct but related neurological disorders could lead to the development of targeted therapies that address the underlying cytoskeletal dysfunction, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
